prompt: What do the β-hydroxy aldehydes and ketones formed in aldol reactions give when heated under acidic or basic conditions?

choices.why: The –OH is lost as water; it isn't oxidized to a carbonyl group.

choices.text: Saturated alcohols with no carbonyl group
choices.why: Heating with acid or base removes water; it doesn't reduce the carbonyl group.
The new C=C forms between the α and β carbons, so it is conjugated with the carbonyl group.

explanation: When heated under either acidic or basic conditions, β-hydroxy aldehydes or ketones dehydrate to α,β-unsaturated products, or conjugated enones (ene + ketone).

prompt: According to the section, what gives the carbonyl condensation reaction its name?

choices.text: Water condenses out when the enone product forms
An alcohol molecule is expelled from the tetrahedral intermediate
choices.why: In the aldol reaction the tetrahedral intermediate is protonated; the molecule lost when the enone forms is water.

choices.text: The reaction must be run cold so that vapors condense
choices.why: Dehydration needs slightly more vigorous conditions, such as a slightly higher temperature, not cooling.

choices.text: The product has fewer carbon atoms than the reactants
choices.why: All the carbons of both partners are kept; only H2O is lost.

explanation: It's the loss of water that gives the carbonyl condensation reaction its name, because water condenses out when an enone product forms.

prompt: Most alcohols resist dehydration by base. Why do aldol products dehydrate easily under basic conditions?

choices.text: Their carbonyl group lets base remove an α hydrogen, and the enolate expels –OH
Hydroxide ion is a good leaving group, so any alcohol dehydrates in base
choices.why: Hydroxide is a poor leaving group, which is why most alcohols resist dehydration by base. The carbonyl group is what makes the difference.

choices.text: The base protonates the –OH group so that it can leave as water
choices.why: A base removes protons; protonating the –OH happens under acidic conditions.

choices.text: Aldol products are always tertiary alcohols, which dehydrate easily
choices.why: Many aldol products, such as 3-hydroxybutanal, are secondary alcohols, and they still dehydrate easily.

explanation: Hydroxide ion is a poor leaving group, so most alcohols resist dehydration by base. In an aldol product, though, base removes an acidic α hydrogen to give an enolate ion, which expels the nearby –OH leaving group.

prompt: By what mechanism do aldol products dehydrate under basic conditions?

choices.why: E1 (or E2) is how water is expelled under acidic conditions, after the –OH is protonated.
E2 is one of the acid-catalyzed pathways. Under basic conditions an enolate ion forms first and then expels –OH.
Nothing is substituted; a C=C double bond forms and the –OH is lost.

explanation: Under basic conditions an acidic α hydrogen is removed, giving an enolate ion that expels the nearby –OH leaving group in an E1cB reaction (Section 11.10). Under acidic conditions, water is expelled in an E1 or E2 reaction instead.

prompt: Under acidic conditions, what forms from the aldol product before its protonated –OH group leaves as water?

choices.why: Enolate ions form under basic conditions, where the dehydration is E1cB.
Enamines come from ketones and secondary amines; no amine is involved here.
Alkoxide ions are anions, which don't form under acidic conditions.

explanation: Under acidic conditions an enol is formed, the –OH group is protonated, and water is expelled in an E1 or E2 reaction. Under basic conditions the intermediate is an enolate ion instead.

prompt: Why are conjugated enones usually obtained directly from aldol reactions, without isolating the β-hydroxy carbonyl compounds?

choices.text: Dehydration needs only slightly more vigorous conditions than aldol formation
β-Hydroxy carbonyl compounds never form as intermediates in aldol reactions
choices.why: They do form; they are the intermediates that then dehydrate.

choices.text: The enone forms first and is then hydrated to the β-hydroxy compound
choices.why: The order is the other way around: the β-hydroxy compound forms first and loses water.

choices.text: Dehydration needs much milder conditions than the aldol reaction itself
choices.why: Dehydration needs slightly more vigorous conditions, not milder ones.

explanation: The conditions needed for aldol dehydration are often only a bit more vigorous (a slightly higher temperature, for instance) than those needed for the aldol reaction itself, so conjugated enones are usually obtained directly.

prompt: What does the section call the real value of aldol dehydration?

choices.text: Removing water drives the aldol equilibrium toward the product
It makes the initial aldol step itself favorable
choices.why: The initial aldol step may still be unfavorable, as it usually is for ketones; the dehydration that follows pulls the equilibrium along.

choices.text: It removes the base catalyst from the mixture
choices.why: Water is removed, not the base.

choices.text: It lets the reaction be run without a base or acid
choices.why: Dehydration happens on heating under either acidic or basic conditions.

explanation: Removing water from the reaction mixture drives the aldol equilibrium toward product. Even when the first aldol step is unfavorable, as it usually is for ketones, the dehydration step lets many aldol condensations be carried out in good yield.

prompt: What percentage yield of cyclohexylidenecyclohexanone does the section report from the aldol condensation of cyclohexanone?
explanation: Cyclohexanone gives cyclohexylidenecyclohexanone in 92% yield, even though the initial aldol equilibrium is unfavorable, because dehydration drives the reaction toward product.

prompt: Cyclohexanone is C6H10O. How many hydrogen atoms does cyclohexylidenecyclohexanone, its aldol condensation product, contain?
explanation: Two cyclohexanone molecules (C12H20O2 in all) combine and lose one H2O, giving C12H18O. So the product has 20 − 2 = 18 hydrogens.

prompt: What enone is obtained from the aldol condensation of acetaldehyde (Worked Example 23.3.1)?

choices.why: That is the β-hydroxy aldehyde intermediate. It loses water to give the enone.
The double bond forms between the α and β carbons, conjugated with the carbonyl group, not at the end of the chain.
The aldehyde group stays an aldehyde, and an enone has a C=C double bond.

explanation: Two acetaldehyde molecules give the β-hydroxy aldehyde, which loses H2O. Two hydrogens come from the α position of one partner and the oxygen from the carbonyl of the other, giving 2-butenal, an α,β-unsaturated aldehyde.

prompt: Acetaldehyde is C2H4O. How many hydrogen atoms does the enone from its aldol condensation contain?
explanation: Two acetaldehyde molecules (C4H8O2) lose one H2O, giving 2-butenal, C4H6O, CH3CH=CHCHO. It has 8 − 2 = 6 hydrogens.

prompt: What enone is expected from the aldol condensation of acetophenone, C6H5COCH3 (Exercise 23.3.1)?

choices.why: That is the β-hydroxy ketone before dehydration. The enone has lost water.
The acceptor carbonyl carbon of acetophenone carries a methyl group, so the β carbon of the product carries CH3, not H.
That C=C is not conjugated with the carbonyl group. The double bond forms between the α and β carbons.

explanation: The α carbon of one acetophenone bonds to the carbonyl carbon of the other, and water is lost to put the C=C between the α and β carbons. The product is 1,3-diphenylbut-2-en-1-one.

prompt: What enone is expected from the aldol condensation of 3-methylbutanal, (CH3)2CHCH2CHO (Exercise 23.3.1)?

choices.why: That is the β-hydroxy aldehyde before dehydration; it has no C=C.
That has only seven carbons. Two molecules of 3-methylbutanal give a ten-carbon product.
That C=C is not conjugated with the carbonyl group. Dehydration puts it between carbons 2 and 3.

explanation: The α carbon of one 3-methylbutanal, which carries an isopropyl group, bonds to the carbonyl carbon of the other. Loss of water gives (CH3)2CHCH2CH=C[CH(CH3)2]CHO, 2-isopropyl-5-methylhex-2-enal.

prompt: What enone is expected from the aldol condensation of cyclopentanone (Exercise 23.3.1)?

choices.why: That is the product from cyclohexanone. Cyclopentanone keeps its five-membered rings.
That is the β-hydroxy ketone before dehydration. The enone has lost water.
That has no C=C bond. The enone has a C=C between the two rings, conjugated with the carbonyl group.

explanation: The α carbon of one cyclopentanone bonds to the carbonyl carbon of the other, and loss of water leaves a C=C between carbon 1 of one ring and carbon 2 of the cyclopentanone: 2-cyclopentylidenecyclopentanone.

prompt: Not counting double-bond isomers, how many enone products does the aldol condensation of 3-methylcyclohexanone give (Exercise 23.3.2)?
explanation: 3-Methylcyclohexanone has two different α carbons, carbon 2 and carbon 6. Either can act as the donor toward the carbonyl of a second molecule, so a mixture of two enone products forms.
